newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to face another mixed day on Wednesday with downside pressure as gold prices restarted their slide after a one-day pause.

"(We'll) probably (get) more of the same from yesterday, although we'll be under pressure again because of the lower gold price...the positive side could be on the pulp and paper side," one trader said.

He said the unveiling late yesterday of extensive restructuring plans at U.S.-based International Paper Co should help fuel interest in Canadian pulp and paper stocks, which have languished for months.
Banks were expected to enjoy a strong day as bonds firmed after a weak day yesterday. But golds were facing another sell-off as Comex prices slid US$3.10 an ounce in New York this morning.

A pause yesterday in gold's slide helped the Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index gain 51.72 points to close at 6580.84. The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared nearly 104 points to reach 7962 and was expected to break through 8000 later today.
The trader said the market's attention has turned to second-quarter corporate earnings, which began rolling out yesterday in the United States with better-than-expected results from Motorola Inc.
The Canadian earnings parade is set to start on Thursday with Alcan Aluminium Ltd.
"So we're going to start that again, and who knows which way they're going to go. But you're probably going to have more downside surprises than upside," the trader said.

In economic news, Canadian housing starts fell by 7.9 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 140,200 units from an unrevised 152,300 units in May, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Wednesday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 155,300 units in June.

* IPL Energy Inc was halted throughout the session on Tuesday. The Calgary-based firm said it bought a 32-percent stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc, thereby making a major push into the province's natural gas business.
